window_weighted_aggregate.method: Per-fold, per-condition MAE averaged across the 5 seeds (each seed's MAE already pooled over that fold's test windows, i.e. window-weighted within-fold), then pooled across all 6 folds weighted by each fold's real test-window count (33,813 windows total). This is the technical/window-level counterpart to the biological-participant-level aggregate below - it lets subjects with more real windows contribute proportionally, rather than each subject counting equally.

heterogeneity_and_sensitivity.window_vs_participant_weighting_agreemen: Window-weighted (A_to_B +0.845, C_to_B +0.920) and biological-participant-level (A_to_B +0.834, C_to_B +0.916) aggregates agree closely (<0.02 bpm difference) - the effect is not an artifact of window-count imbalance across subjects. (Participant-level C_to_B corrected from a HIGH-01 evaluation bug this sprint; see high01_participant_c_correction_note.)
heterogeneity_and_sensitivity.note_on_direction_vs_bounded_diagnostic: The prior bounded single-fold diagnostic (fold 5 only, 3/3 subjects favored B for both A_to_B and C_to_B, confirmed after the HIGH-01 per-subject-C fix) showed a larger effect (A_cap->B ~+1.342, C->B ~+1.629, both from the always-correct fold-level/seed-pooled evaluation, unaffected by HIGH-01) than the full 6-fold result (A_cap->B ~+0.834-0.845, C->B ~+0.916-0.920). Direction is consistent (B favored) at both the aggregate and majority-subject level, but the full cohort reveals real subject heterogeneity (6/18 subjects favor A_cap over B, 5/18 favor C over B) that the single fold's 3/3-favor-B result did not surface - this is exactly the kind of dilution a bounded diagnostic cannot rule out, and is why the master prompt required the full CV before any final classification.

final_classification_rationale: Aggregate MAE gap favors B at both the participant-level (A_cap->B +0.834 bpm, C->B +0.916 bpm, n=18) and window-weighted level (A_cap->B +0.845 bpm, C->B +0.920 bpm, 33,813 pooled test windows), with no sign reversal under either aggregation or under leave-one-out exclusion of the single most extreme subject (P16 for A_to_B, P04 for C_to_B). A majority of subjects favor B under both comparisons (12/18 for A_cap->B, 13/18 for C->B). This is directionally consistent with the prior bounded single-fold diagnostic and with the capacity-controlled PPG-DaLiA finding, though the full cohort's real heterogeneity (6/18 and 5/18 subjects respectively favor the opposite direction) means this is a real but moderate, heterogeneous effect - not a uniform one. Classified SUPPORTIVE rather than MIXED because no analysis performed (window-weighted, participant-level, or leave-one-out) reversed the aggregate sign. (Condition C's participant-level values were corrected this sprint under HIGH-01 remediation - see high01_participant_c_correction_note; the classification and its underlying direction were unchanged by the correction.)
